questions.question: Vasudeva I who issued coins in gold (dinars and quarter dinars) and copper (single denomination) was a ______ king.
questions.solution:
Kushana
Vasudeva I was the last of the "Great Kushans." He ruled in Northern India and Central Asia, where he minted coins in the city of Balkh. The Kushana dynasty was founded by Kujula Kadphises.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sanskrit historical poem Ramacharita by Sandhyakar Nandi:
1. The hero of the poem Ramacharita is Ramapala, the 15th ruler of the Pala dynasty.
2. Sandhyakar Nandi was patronized by the Gupta ruler Samudragupta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 only
Ramapala was the successor to the Pala king Shurapala II in the Bengal region of the Indian subcontinent, and 15th ruler of the Pala line. Sandhyakar Nandi was patronized by Madanapala, ruler of Pala Dynasty, not Samudragupta.

questions.question: Vindhyashakti was the founder of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
Vakataka dynasty
It originated from the Deccan in the mid-3rd century CE. Vakatakas were the most important successors of the Satavahanas in the Deccan and coexistent with the Guptas in northern India.

questions.question: An inscription, Takht-i-Bahi recovered from Mardan near Peshawar, indicates the rule of which of the following dynasties in north-western area of present Pakistan?
questions.solution:
Parthians (247 BC - 224 AD)
It was founded by Arsaces I of Parthia when he rebelled against the Seleucid Empire. They replaced the Sakas in North-Western India. The Takht-i-Bahi inscription, dated in 45 AD, refers to Gondophenes as a Parthian ruler.

questions.question: The Maukharis ruled over which of the following cities in western Uttar Pradesh that over time replaced Pataliputra as a political centre of north India?
questions.solution:
Kannauj
The Maukharis, initially vassals of the Guptas and titled Samantas, gained independence in the mid-6th century as the Gupta Empire declined.

questions.question: Under which of the following Pala king's patronage was the Vikramshila university in 8th century India founded?
questions.solution:
Dharmapala
The second ruler of the Pala Dynasty, ascended the throne around 780 AD after Gopala and expanded the empire significantly. He defeated Indrayudha of Kanauj, installing Chakrayudha as his nominee, but later faced defeat by Rashtrakuta king Dhruva near Monghyr, Bihar.

questions.question: Three Poets Pampa, Ponna and Ranna are called as the 'Three Jewels' of:
questions.solution:
Kannada Literature
  • Pampa, also known as Adi Pampa, is renowned for his literary works, including "Vikramarjuna Vijaya" and "Adi Purana"
  • Ponna, often referred to as Ponna Kavishwara, served as a court poet for Rashtrakuta king Krishna III and is best known for his epic "Shantipurana"
  • Ranna was a court poet of the Western Chalukya Empire, and his most celebrated work is "Gadayuddha"

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Satavahana administration:
1. The Satavahana kingdom was divided into subdivisions called Aharas or Rashtrakas, which meant districts.
2. The Satavahana administration used only cash as a mode of revenue collection.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 only
Satavahana: Period: 60 BC - 225 AD; Capital - Pratishthana (Paithan) and Amravati; Founder - Simuka. The lowest level of administration was a grama which was under the charge of a Gramika. There were also officers called amatyas who were perhaps ministers or advisors of the king. Revenue was collected both in cash and kind. It majorly comprised present Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Maharashtra.

questions.question: ______, authored by Tolkappiyar, is the earliest Tamil literature.
questions.solution:
Tolkappiyam
Tamil has a literary tradition that goes back to the period of the Sangams. The most well-known surviving works from this period are the Tolkappiyam (a book of grammar attributed to Tolkappiyar), Ettu Togai (Eight Anthologies), Pattu Pattu (Ten Idylls).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pandya Kingdom:
Statement 1: The Pandya Kingdom was first mentioned by Megasthenes, who said that it was famous for pearls.
Statement 2: The capital of the Pandya Kingdom was Madurai.
questions.option_1: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 correctly explains Statement 1
questions.option_2: Both statements are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Both statements are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1
Megasthenes: A Greek diplomat and historian who mentioned the Pandya Kingdom in his book Indica around 300 BCE. The Pandya Kingdom was an ancient Tamil kingdom that ruled parts of southern India, especially Tamil Nadu, from the 6th century BCE to the 15th century CE.

questions.question: In peninsular India, which of the following kingdoms was the local power that ruled over northern Maharashtra and Vidarbha?
questions.solution:
Vakatakas
Vindhyashakti founded the Vakataka dynasty in the third century. Their history is mainly known through land grant charters issued to Brahmanas. The Maukhari dynasty ruled over (modern day) Uttar Pradesh and parts of Bihar.

questions.question: In 10th century India, Queen Didda became the ruler of which of the following regions of north India?
questions.solution:
Kashmir
Didda was the ruler of Kashmir from 980 CE to 1003 CE. Most knowledge relating to Didda is obtained from the Rajatarangini. Ashish Kaul's novel Didda: The Warrior Queen of Kashmir is based on Didda's life.

questions.question: Mahendravarman I who wrote Mattavilasa-prahasana is related to which of the following ruling dynasties?
questions.solution:
Pallava dynasty (275 CE to 897 CE)
They ruled a significant portion of the Deccan, also known as Tondaimandalam, which covered parts of present-day Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. Founder - Simha Vishnu (Avanisimha).

questions.question: The Pratiharas who first had their capital at Bhinmal gained prominence during the rule of:
questions.solution:
Nagabhatta I (Reign: 730-760 AD)
He laid the foundation of the Pratihara dynasty's power. He is best known for defeating the Arabs during their expansion and building an empire that stretched from Gujarat to Gwalior, stopping further Arab invasions in eastern Sindh.

questions.question: According to the inscriptions, Pushyamitra Shunga was a devotee of which of the following Gods?
questions.solution:
Krishna
Pushyamitra Shunga founded the Shunga Empire after assassinating the last Mauryan emperor, Brihadratha Maurya. He ruled from 184 BC to 75 BC, driving out the Greeks through the Shunga-Greek war. The capital of the Shunga Empire was Pataliputra.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pallava Chalukya conflict:
Statement 1: Pallava king Narasimhavarman I defeated Pulakesin II of the Chalukya dynasty around 642 CE.
Statement 2: After this victory, the Pallavas captured the Chalukya capital, Vatapi (Badami), and Narasimhavarman earned the title 'Vatapikonda.'
questions.option_1: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 correctly explains Statement 1
questions.option_2: Both statements are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Both statements are true, and Statement 2 correctly explains Statement 1
Pulakesin II, a ruler of the Chalukya dynasty, reigned from 610 CE to 642 CE, expanding his empire across much of the Deccan region. However, in 642-643 CE, Pallava king Narasimha Varman I defeated Pulakesin II when his general, Shiruttondar Paranjoti, captured the Chalukya capital, Vatapi. Simhavishnu is regarded as the founder of the Pallava dynasty, a Tamil dynasty that ruled parts of South India from the 3rd to the 9th century.

questions.question: In the context of Mathura school of Art, during which of the following periods were a number of sculptures of Brahmanical deities, such as Kartikeya, Vishnu and Kubera carved?
questions.solution:
Kushana
The Kushan Empire was a syncretic empire established by the Yuezhi in the Bactrian territories in the early 1st century. The Mathura School of Art flourished under the Kushana emperor Kanishka during the first century AD.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Badami (Vatapi) Chalukyas:
Statement 1: The Chalukyas of Badami were originally subjects of the Kadambas of Banavasi.
Statement 2: The Chalukyas established their capital at Kanchipuram after gaining independence.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
The Kadambas ruled from Banavasi in present-day Karnataka, marking a significant period in the early medieval history of the Deccan region. Badami was the capital of the early Chalukyan dynasty, which governed the area from 543 to 598 CE. With the decline of the Vakataka rule, the Chalukyas established their dominance in the Deccan.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Pala Dynasty of eastern India is INCORRECT?
questions.option_1: Devapala was the grandson of Gopala.
questions.option_3: The Pala kings were the followers of Buddhism.
questions.option_4: The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala.
questions.solution:
Dharmapala founded the Valabhi university
The Vallabhi University was founded by Bhattarka, the king of the Maitraka Empire, not Dharmapala. Pala Dynasty: The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala, probably around 750 AD. Dharmapala was the second ruler of the Pala Empire.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers was a part of the Tripartite Struggle for the possession of Kannauj?
questions.solution:
Dharmapala
The Tripartite Struggle, also known as the Kannauj Triangle Wars, took place in the 8th and 9th centuries, between the three dynasties - The Palas of Bengal, The Pratiharas of Central India and The Rashtrakutas of Deccan.

questions.question: The founder of the Pallava dynasty was:
questions.solution:
Simhavishnu (575-590 AD)
He was the first Pallava monarch whose domain extended beyond Kanchipuram (Kanchi) in the South. Rise: Defeating Kalabhras inaugurated the rule of imperial Pallavas. Royal Titles: Avanisimha (lion of the Earth). His court poet Bharavi - Wrote Kiratarjuniya.

questions.question: Bilhana was a court poet in which of the following kingdoms?
questions.solution:
Vikramaditya VI
The Chalukya dynasty was established by Pulakeshin I in 543. He took Vatapi (modern Badami in Bagalkot district, Karnataka) under his control and made it his capital. He and his descendants are referred to as "Chalukyas of Badami".

questions.question: Which of the following was the port-city of the Pandyan Kingdom?
questions.solution:
Korkai
Pandya dynasty (4th century BCE to the 17th century CE): Capital - Madurai, Founder - Mudathirumaran.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Dantidurga:
Statement 1: Dantidurga, also known as Dantivarman, was the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty.
Statement 2: The Rashtrakuta capital under Dantidurga was established at Kanchipuram.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
Manyakheta was the capital of the Rashtrakuta kingdom. The Eichpur clan, initially a feudatory of the Badami Chalukyas, rose to power under Dantidurga by overthrowing Chalukya ruler Kirtivarman II and establishing an empire in the Gulbarga region. This clan became known as the Rashtrakutas of Manyakheta, who emerged as a significant power in Maharashtra-Karnataka region.

questions.question: Krishna III of Rashtrakuta dynasty established a victory pillar and a temple at which of the following cities of south India after defeating the Chola ruler Parantaka I?
questions.solution:
Rameswaram
Krishna III whose Kannada name was Kannara (939-967 C.E.) was the last great warrior and able monarch of the Rashtrakuta dynasty (Founder: Dantivarman). Its Capital - Manyakheta. Parantaka I was known as the destroyer of Madurai (the capital city of the Pandyas).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Telugu literature:
Statement 1: Nanniah, known as the Adi Kavi of Telugu literature, began the translation of the Mahabharata into Telugu.
Statement 2: Nanniah undertook this work under the patronage of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
Nanniah (Nannayya) is regarded as the first poet of Telugu literature and is part of the famous "Trinity of Poets" (comprising Nannaya, Tikkana and Erra Pragada) in Telugu literature. He began the translation of the Mahabharata from Sanskrit into Telugu during the 11th century under the patronage of the Eastern Chalukya king, Rajaraja Narendra, not Pallava king.

questions.question: Manyakheta or Malkhed was the capital of which of the following kingdoms?
questions.solution:
Rashtrakuta
Dantidurga was the founder of the Rashtrakuta empire who fixed his capital at Manyakheta or Malkhed near modern Sholapur.

questions.question: During the reign of which of the Pallava kings was the shore temple at Mahabalipuram built?
questions.solution:
Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha
He ruled the Pallava dynasty from 700 to 728 CE. He also constructed the Kailasanatha Temple in Kanchipuram.

questions.question: Rajatarangini, the book authored by Kalhana in 12th Century was originally written in which of the following languages?
questions.solution:
Sanskrit
The word "Rajatarangini" means "River of Kings." This book chronicles the history of the northwestern Indian subcontinent, specifically the kings of Kashmir. It contains 7,826 verses divided into eight sections known as Tarangas (waves).

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty in the region of Malwa in the eighth century?
questions.solution:
Nagabhatta I
The Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty (8th-11th Century A.D.) ruled over northern and western India. Nagabhatta I established an empire extending from Gujarat to Gwalior and defied the Arab invasions towards further east of Sindh.
